claims.visible_claim: The Big Five is one of the most widely studied dimensional models in personality psychology. It organizes personality descriptions into five broad domains: Openness to Experience, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism, often abbreviated as OCEAN ([S1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2283588/)). Each domain is continuous. A result does not assign you to an “X type”; it estimates how strongly a set of tendencies tends to appear.
claims.boundary: Supports the broad model structure, not FermatMind product validity, norms, or individual prediction.
claims.source_section: What Is the Big Five Personality Model?

claims.visible_claim: This page grounds its description of the five broad domains in lexical research on the five-factor structure ([S1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2283588/)). There is no single universal hierarchy beneath those domains: the BFI-2, for example, uses 15 facets ([S2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27055049/)), while the official IPIP resource lists several scales designed to measure constructs similar to the 30 NEO facets ([S11](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm)). The 30-facet vocabulary in this package is therefore an explicitly labeled NEO/IPIP-NEO interpretive framework, not the only facet structure shared by every Big Five instrument.
claims.boundary: Different Big Five and FFM instruments must not be treated as hierarchically or psychometrically equivalent.
claims.scientific_narrowing_reason: The English wording makes the non-equivalence of instruments and the interpretive-only role of the 30-facet vocabulary explicit.

claims.visible_claim: - **Hiring screening:** Meta-analytic evidence indicates that group-level associations between Big Five traits and performance outcomes vary by trait and outcome. That evidence cannot be converted into a prediction of one person’s success, job fit, or work performance, and it is not evidence that FermatMind is valid for hiring ([S9](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jopy.12683)).
claims.boundary: Group-level associations do not establish individual success, occupational fit, hiring utility, or FermatMind product validity.
claims.source_section: Uses the Big Five Cannot Support
claims.scientific_narrowing_reason: The English sentence explicitly separates meta-analytic group associations from individual and product-level inference.

claims.visible_claim: Group-level longitudinal evidence and individual interpretation must be kept separate when discussing personality change ([S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16435954/)).
claims.boundary: Does not predict an individual, facet, fixed age point, retest interval, or intervention effect.
claims.source_section: How to Understand Stability and Change

claims.visible_claim: A meta-analysis of longitudinal studies reported average changes in some personality traits across the life course, but those results describe sample averages, not a timetable for any one person ([S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16435954/)).
claims.boundary: Sample-average change cannot be converted into an individual timetable or facet forecast.
claims.source_section: How to Understand Stability and Change
claims.scientific_narrowing_reason: The wording foregrounds the sample-average boundary before any practical interpretation.

claims.visible_claim: Meta-analytic longitudinal research reports group-average changes in some personality traits across the life course, but it cannot predict how a particular person, a particular facet, or a fixed age point will change ([S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16435954/)).
claims.boundary: Does not establish an individual change path, facet-specific rate, or fixed retest schedule.
claims.scientific_narrowing_reason: The answer preserves the finding while explicitly blocking person, facet, and fixed-age prediction.

claims.visible_claim: The lexical research tradition used personality-descriptive words and factor analysis to identify five broad factors ([S1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2283588/)). Instruments use different items and hierarchical structures, so research on the general model does not automatically validate a specific product, translation, norm, or score interpretation.
claims.boundary: General model research does not establish product validity, translation validity, norms, or individual prediction.
claims.scientific_narrowing_reason: The answer makes the model-to-product inference boundary explicit for an English reader.

claims.visible_claim: FermatMind has not published product-level reliability, validity, Chinese norms, or individual predictive evidence for the scores discussed by this package. This material is for self-observation and education. It is not for clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, school admission, or replacing a career decision.
claims.boundary: Public method boundary; not an empirical research claim or endorsement.
